4|Abiraterone plus prednisone added to androgen deprivation
5|therapy and docetaxel in de novo metastatic castration-
6|sensitive prostate cancer (PEACE-1): a multicentre, open-
7|label, randomised, phase 3 study with a 2 × 2 factorial design
8|Karim Fizazi, Stéphanie Foulon, Joan Carles, Guilhem Roubaud, Ray McDermott, Aude Fléchon, Bertrand Tombal, Stéphane Supiot,
9|Dominik Berthold, Philippe Ronchin, Gabriel Kacso, Gwenaëlle Gravis, Fabio Calabro, Jean-François Berdah, Ali Hasbini, Marlon Silva,
10|Antoine Thiery-Vuillemin, Igor Latorzeff, Loïc Mourey, Brigitte Laguerre, Sophie Abadie-Lacourtoisie, Etienne Martin, Claude El Kouri,
11|Anne Escande, Alvar Rosello, Nicolas Magne, Friederike Schlurmann, Frank Priou, Marie-Eve Chand-Fouche, Salvador Villà Freixa,
12|Muhammad Jamaluddin, Isabelle Rieger, Alberto Bossi, on behalf of the PEACE-1 investigators*
13|Summary
14|Background Current standard of care for metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer supplements androgen
15|deprivation therapy with either docetaxel, second-generation hormonal therapy, or radiotherapy. We aimed to
16|evaluate the efficacy and safety of abiraterone plus prednisone, with or without radiotherapy, in addition to
17|standard of care.
18|Methods We conducted an open-label, randomised, phase 3 study with a 2 × 2 factorial design (PEACE-1) at
19|77 hospitals across Belgium, France, Ireland, Italy, Romania, Spain, and Switzerland. Eligible patients were male,
20|aged 18 years or older, with histologically confirmed or cytologically confirmed de novo metastatic prostate
21|adenocarcinoma, and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-1 (or 2 due to bone pain).
22|Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) to standard of care (androgen deprivation therapy alone or with
23|intravenous docetaxel 75 mg/m2 once every 3 weeks), standard of care plus radiotherapy, standard of care plus
24|abiraterone (oral 1000 mg abiraterone once daily plus oral 5 mg prednisone twice daily), or standard of care plus
25|radiotherapy plus abiraterone. Neither the investigators nor the patients were masked to treatment allocation. The
26|coprimary endpoints were radiographic progression-free survival and overall survival. Abiraterone efficacy was
27|first assessed in the overall population and then in the population who received androgen deprivation therapy
28|with docetaxel as standard of care (population of interest). This study is ongoing and is registered with
29|ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT01957436.
30|Findings Between Nov 27, 2013, and Dec 20, 2018, 1173 patients were enrolled (one patient subsequently withdrew
31|consent for analysis of his data) and assigned to receive standard of care (n=296), standard of care plus radiotherapy
32|(n=293), standard of care plus abiraterone (n=292), or standard of care plus radiotherapy plus abiraterone (n=291).
33|Median follow-up was 3·5 years (IQR 2·8-4·6) for radiographic progression-free survival and 4·4 years (3·5-5·4)
34|for overall survival. Adjusted Cox regression modelling revealed no interaction between abiraterone and
35|radiotherapy, enabling the pooled analysis of abiraterone efficacy. In the overall population, patients assigned to
36|receive abiraterone (n=583) had longer radiographic progression-free survival (hazard ratio [HR] 0·54, 99·9% CI
37|0·41-0·71; p<0·0001) and overall survival (0·82, 95·1% CI 0·69-0·98; p=0·030) than patients who did not receive
38|abiraterone (n=589). In the androgen deprivation therapy with docetaxel population (n=355 in both with
39|abiraterone and without abiraterone groups), the HRs were consistent (radiographic progression-free survival 0·50,
40|99·9% CI 0·34-0·71; p<0·0001; overall survival 0·75, 95·1% CI 0·59-0·95; p=0·017). In the androgen deprivation
41|therapy with docetaxel population, grade 3 or worse adverse events occurred in 217 (63%) of 347 patients who
42|received abiraterone and 181 (52%) of 350 who did not; hypertension had the largest difference in occurrence
43|(76 [22%] patients and 45 [13%], respectively). Addition of abiraterone to androgen deprivation therapy plus
44|docetaxel did not increase the rates of neutropenia, febrile neutropenia, fatigue, or neuropathy compared with
45|androgen deprivation therapy plus docetaxel alone.
46|Interpretation Combining androgen deprivation therapy, docetaxel, and abiraterone in de novo metastatic castration-
47|sensitive prostate cancer improved overall survival and radiographic progression-free survival with a modest increase
48|in toxicity, mostly hypertension. This triplet therapy could become a standard of care for these patients.

62|Introduction
63|After several decades with no substantial progress, the
64|treatment of de novo (synchronous) metastatic prostate
65|cancer has drastically evolved in the past 10 years
66|with the addition of diverse treatments to androgen
67|deprivation therapy (ADT), the former standard of care
68|(SOC). The prognosis for men with de novo metastatic
69|castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC) has been
70|improved by using ADT concomitantly with either
71|docetaxel1-5 or one of the second-generation androgen
72|receptor axis inhibitors (abiraterone,6-8 apalutamide,9 or
73|enzalutamide10,11). In 2018, radiotherapy to the primary
74|tumour was also shown to extend the overall survival of
75|patients with low-volume metastatic burden.12 The
76|benefits of these various combinatory therapies were
77|confirmed by meta-analyses13-15 and have helped to shape
78|the current guidelines for the treatment of mCSPC.16-18
79|Nevertheless, it remains to be established whether
80|merging some of these new therapies could provide
81|further clinical benefits and, if so, what combination
82|might be most suitable for de novo mCSPC.19 Conducted
83|by a European consortium (PEACE),20 this study aimed to
84|evaluate the efficacy and safety of abiraterone plus
85|prednisone, with or without radiotherapy, in addition to
86|SOC (ADT with or without docetaxel).
87|Methods
88|Study design and participants
89|We conducted an open-label, randomised, active-
90|controlled, phase 3 study with a 2 × 2 factorial design
91|(PEACE-1) at 77 sites across seven European countries
92|(Belgium, France, Ireland, Italy, Romania, Spain, and
93|Switzerland). The complete list of inclusion and exclusion
94|criteria is provided in the appendix (pp 5-6). Briefly, male
95|patients aged 18 years or older with histologically confirmed
96|or cytologically confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma
97|documented as de novo metastatic by bone scan, CT, or
98|MRI (according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid
99|Tumors [RECIST] version 1.1 criteria) and an Eastern
100|Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status
101|of 0-1 (or 2 due to bone pain) were eligible for inclusion,
102|provided they had received ADT for no more than
103|3 months before randomisation and had at least 6 weeks
104|between the initiation of ADT and the first docetaxel
105|dose. Patients with a pure small-cell carcinoma, or
106|previous prostate cancer treated by a definitive local
107|treatment were not eligible. All participants provided
108|written informed consent before any study-specific
109|procedures or randomisation were initiated.
110|The initial protocol was reviewed and first approved on
111|July 10, 2013, by the French Independent Ethics
112|Committee (Comité de Protection des Personnes Ile de
113|France VII). The protocol complied with the ethical
114|principles of the Declaration of Helsinki and was
115|approved by Institutional Review Boards at each study
116|site. The trial conformed with the International
117|Conference on Harmonization and Good Clinical
118|Practice guidelines, and applicable regulatory require
119|ments. Steering and Independent Data Monitoring
120|Committees roles and members are described in the
121|appendix (pp 3-4).
122|Two major protocol amendments were made during
123|the accrual period, to account for the evolution of SOC
124|for men with mCSPC. Although ADT alone was the SOC
125|when the trial began recruitment in 2013, the protocol
126|was amended on Oct 5, 2015 (273 patients had already
127|been accrued), to allow for docetaxel use in SOC
128|worldwide, after ADT with docetaxel had shown
129|improvement in overall survival.2,3 Then, in 2017, ADT
130|plus abiraterone was also shown to improve overall
131|Research in context
132|Evidence before this study
133|We searched PubMed from Jan 1, 1984, to Dec 31, 2012, for
134|papers in English, using the terms "prostate cancer",
135|"metastases", and "phase 3 trial", and found 16 studies. When
136|the PEACE-1 trial began in 2013, androgen deprivation
137|therapy (ADT) had for several decades been the standard of
138|care for men with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate
139|cancer (mCSPC). All randomised trials conducted before the
140|mid-2010s had not shown improvement in outcomes with
141|new therapies compared with ADT. During recruitment for the
142|PEACE-1 trial (2013-18), overall survival of patients with de
143|novo mCSPC was shown to be improved by combining ADT
144|with either docetaxel or one of the second-generation
145|androgen receptor axis inhibitors (abiraterone, apalutamide,
146|or enzalutamide) and radiotherapy to the primary tumour, in
147|men with low metastatic burden. It had not yet been shown
148|whether combining some of these new therapies with ADT in
149|triple therapy could provide further clinical benefits.
150|Added value of this study
151|To our knowledge, PEACE-1 is the first trial to show that
152|a triple systemic therapy-consisting of ADT, docetaxel,
153|and a second-generation androgen signalling inhibitor
154|(abiraterone, combined with prednisone)-improves both
155|radiographic progression-free survival and overall survival in
156|patients with de novo mCSPC, without excessively increasing
157|toxicity (mostly hypertension and aminotransferase increase).
158|Implications of all the available evidence
159|The findings from the PEACE-1 trial, combined with the evidence
160|from other studies, add weight to the concept that systemic
161|treatment intensification provides clinical benefit for men with
162|mCSPC and illustrate that early treatment intensification is more
163|effective than identical or similar treatments being used
164|sequentially when the disease has become castration-resistant.
165|At a minimum, patients with mCSPC with a high metastatic
166|burden who are fit enough to be treated with docetaxel should
167|be considered for this triple systemic therapy.

4|survival compared with ADT alone.6,7 Thereby, an
5|additional amendment was filed on Aug 10, 2017, to make
6|docetaxel mandatory for the remainder of the patients to
7|be accrued, so that the trial could evaluate the addition of
8|abiraterone to ADT with docetaxel (given that the
9|evaluation of ADT plus abiraterone compared with ADT
10|alone had already been addressed by other trials). Further
11|details on the amendments to the protocol and statistical
12|analysis plan are provided in the appendix (pp 7-8).
13|Evolution of the sample size and allocation of patients
14|according to these key amendments is depicted in the
15|appendix (pp 9-10).
16|Randomisation and masking
17|Eligible patients were centrally randomly assigned in the
18|Alea Clinical Portal), in a 1:1:1:1 ratio, to SOC, SOC plus
19|radiotherapy, SOC plus abiraterone (abiraterone plus
20|prednisone), or SOC plus radiotherapy plus abiraterone.
21|This randomisation process was performed via the
22|Tenalea autonomous software, solely accessed by the trial
23|data manager within the Epidemioloy and Biostatistics
24|facility of the Gustave Roussy Center in Villejuif, France
25|until 2015, then by each investigator.
26|Randomisation was done using a minimisation
27|algorithm, stratified by study site, ECOG performance
28|status (0 vs 1-2), type of ADT (gonadotropin-releasing
29|hormone agonist vs antagonist vs bilateral orchiectomy),
30|planned administration of docetaxel (yes vs no), and
31|disease extent or burden based on metastatic status
32|(lymph node metastases only vs bone metastases [with or
33|without lymph node metastases] vs visceral metastases).
34|A similar weight was given to each of the five
35|stratification factors, with 80% probability to minimise
36|imbalance in the number of patients assigned to each
37|treatment group. As the case report form gathered
38|information for patient stratification according to
39|high-volume versus low-volume metastatic burden
40|classification (as defined in the CHAARTED study2 [high
41|volume was defined as the presence of visceral
42|metastases or at least four bone lesions with one beyond
43|the vertebral bodies and pelvis]), this later classification
44|was retained to enable inter-trial comparisons. No
45|masking was performed in this study.
46|Procedures
47|In all patients in the study, ADT was planned to be
48|continuously maintained by either a gonadotropin-
49|releasing hormone agonist or antagonist, or bilateral
50|orchiectomy. Patients assigned to receive docetaxel as part
51|of SOC with continuous ADT were to receive six cycles of
52|intravenous docetaxel (75 mg/m2 per cycle; maximum
53|dose of 150 mg per cycle), to be administered every
54|3 weeks (plus or minus 3 days). Granulocyte colony-
55|stimulating factor (G-CSF) injections after each docetaxel
56|cycle were recommended until the protocol amendment
57|on Jan 22, 2018, made G-CSF prophylaxis mandatory for
58|patients who received docetaxel. The first docetaxel cycle
59|had to be administered within 14 days after randomisation
60|and be at least 6 weeks after ADT initiation. Patients
61|assigned to receive abiraterone received 1000 mg of
62|abiraterone (four 250 mg tablets, orally) once daily plus
63|prednisone 5 mg orally twice daily, starting within 6 weeks
64|after ADT initiation. PEACE-1 began accrual in 2013,
65|before the LATITUDE6 and the STAMPEDE7 abiraterone
66|trials were reported and before abiraterone was approved
67|for mCSPC, which is why we used 10 mg of prednisone,
68|similar to what is approved for metastatic castration-
69|resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). Abiraterone and
70|prednisone (hereafter referred to as abiraterone) were
71|administered until disease progression to castration
72|resistance, withdrawal of consent, unacceptable toxicity,
73|or death. Patients assigned to receive radiotherapy
74|(74 Gy in 37 fractions administered over 7-8 weeks)
75|were planned to start radiotherapy at least 3 weeks
76|after docetaxel completion (but no more than 8 weeks
77|after completion). Treatments given after disease
78|progression followed common practice, and investigators
79|were able to change therapy as they thought was most
80|appropriate, on the basis of prostate-specific antigen
81|(PSA) concentration variation or clinical progression,
82|even in absence of radiographical evidence. The treatment
83|flow chart is depicted in the appendix (p 10).
84|Every enrolled patient was to be followed-up for a
85|duration of 10 years. The complete list of assessments
86|performed at each visit and follow-up intervals are
87|detailed in the appendix (pp 12-13). Survival status data
88|were gathered within 3 months of the cutoff date for
89|97% of patients.
90|Outcomes
91|The coprimary endpoints were radiographic progression-
92|free survival and overall survival. Radiographical pro
93|gression of soft-tissue lesions was evaluated by either CT
94|or MRI, on the basis of RECIST version 1.1. Progression
95|of bone lesions was assessed by bone scan according to
96|the adapted version of Prostate Cancer Working Group 2
97|criteria,21 with no secondary bone scan required to
98|confirm progression. Radiographic progression-free
99|survival was defined as the time between randomisation
100|and the occurrence of radiographical progression or
101|death from any cause. Overall survival was defined as the
102|time between randomisation and death from any cause.
103|Patients without events were censored at the date of last
104|follow-up.
105|The secondary endpoints were castration-resistant
106|prostate cancer (CRPC)-free survival, serious-genito
107|urinary-event-free survival, prostate-cancer-specific survival,
108|time to next skeletal-related event, PSA response rate,
109|prognostic study of serum PSA measured 6-8 months
110|after initiation of systemic therapy, time to pain pro
111|gression, time to chemotherapy for CRPC, quality of life,
112|changes in bone mineral density, correlation of biomarkers
113|with outcome, event rate per 100 person-years of treatment
114|analysis, and toxicity. CRPC-free survival was defined as

26|Statistical analysis
27|The initial protocol in 2013 planned for a sample size of
28|916 patients. However, due to a change in the SOC and the
29|knowledge gained from the LATITUDE and STAMPEDE
30|trial results published in late 2017, the planned sample
31|size was increased to 1173 and the coprimary study aims
32|were revised (appendix pp 7-8). Because PEACE-1 was the
33|only phase 3 trial to date that could determine abiraterone
34|efficacy in patients with mCSPC receiving ADT plus
35|docetaxel as SOC, the timing of the final analyses was
36|based on this population (population of interest). Sample
37|size calculation was performed with East software (Cytel;
38|Cambridge, MA, USA), on the basis of the assumption
39|that no significant interaction would take place between
40|radiotherapy and abiraterone, to allow for a 2 × 2 factorial
41|analysis of abiraterone efficacy. For abiraterone efficacy
42|evaluation, the predetermined acceptable probability of a
43|type I error was set at 0·05, divided between the two
44|coprimary endpoints (0·049 for overall survival and 0·001
45|for
46|radiographic
47|progression-free
48|survival).
49|We
50|hypothesised that adding abiraterone to ADT plus
51|docetaxel would improve overall survival by 30% over a
52|median of 53 months and progression-free survival by
53|40% over 30 months. Hence, with 355 patients assigned to
54|ADT with docetaxel plus abiraterone (with or without
55|radiotherapy) and 355 patients assigned to ADT with
56|docetaxel
57|without
58|abiraterone
59|(with
60|or
61|without
62|radiotherapy), 249 deaths would give an 80% power to
63|detect an overall survival hazard ratio (HR) of 0·70 at a
64|two-sided α level of 0·049. With the same group allocation,
65|262 radiographic progression events or deaths were
66|predicted to have an 80% power to detect a radiographic
67|progression-free survival HR of 0·60 at a two-sided α level
68|of 0·001.
69|This trial had a factorial design, based on the
70|assumption that there would be no interaction between
71|abiraterone and radiotherapy. Before analysing the
72|various outcomes, the presence of such an interaction
73|for both coprimary endpoints was tested by analyses of
74|maximum likelihood estimates using a Cox model
75|adjusted for stratification factors (ECOG performance
76|status [0 vs 1-2], ADT type [gonadotropin-releasing
77|hormone agonist vs antagonist vs bilateral orchiectomy],
78|metastatic burden [low vs high; as defined in the
79|Randomisation and masking section],2 and docetaxel
80|[no docetaxel before amendment vs no docetaxel after
81|amendment vs with docetaxel after amendment]). In the
82|absence of a qualitative interaction (p>0·05) between
83|abiraterone and radiotherapy, the groups were to be
84|combined two by two on the basis of abiraterone
85|administration, regardless of radiotherapy, before se
86|quentially assessing abiraterone efficacy first in the
87|overall population and then in the ADT with docetaxel
88|population (assuming the significance level was reached
89|in first instance). As the preplanned number of pro
90|gression-free survival and overall survival events had
91|not been reached in the study population at the time
92|this paper was written, the efficacy of radiotherapy
93|remains to be analysed (appendix p 16). The coprimary
94|endpoint results presented here correspond to the final
95|planned analysis; no interim analysis was conducted.
96|All efficacy analyses were conducted in the intention-to-
97|treat population, defined as all patients who were
98|randomly assigned to a treatment group. Safety analyses
99|were conducted in the safety population, according to
100|the treatment actually received by the patients (those
101|who did not receive any investigational treatment were
102|not included in the safety analyses).
103|The median follow-up was estimated by the inverse
104|Kaplan-Meier method. Time-to-event endpoints were
105|estimated by the Kaplan-Meier method. The Cox
106|proportional hazards model adjusted for radiotherapy
107|and stratification factors provided significances and an
108|estimate of the abiraterone effect (p value and HR with
109|CIs adjusted to match adjustment made to significance
110|levels in the corresponding test [ie, 99·9% for
111|radiographic progression-free survival, 95·1% for overall
112|survival, and 95% for secondary endpoints]). The
113|assumption of proportional hazards was evaluated on
114|the basis of the weighted Schoenfeld residuals. The
115|heterogeneity of the effect of abiraterone in the
116|predefined stratification subgroups was evaluated using
117|Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for radio
118|therapy and stratification factors and including an
119|interaction term between abiraterone and the studied
120|stratification variable. These analyses are illustrated
121|using forest plots. Notably, we analysed the efficacy of
122|abiraterone in the ADT with docetaxel population by
123|disease burden. Non-parametric CIs for the median
124|survival differences between groups were analysed by
125|the bootkm function of the R Hmisc package

12|Results
13|Between Nov 27, 2013, and Dec 20, 2018, 1173 patients
14|were enrolled (one patient subsequently withdrew
15|consent for analysis of his data) and assigned to receive
16|SOC (n=296), SOC plus radiotherapy (n=293), SOC plus
17|abiraterone (n=292), or SOC plus radiotherapy plus
18|abiraterone (n=291; figure 1). SOC was ADT alone in
19|462 patients and ADT with docetaxel in 710 patients
20|(table 1).
21|For radiographic progression-free survival and overall
22|survival, the median follow-up periods were longer in
23|the overall population (3·5 years [IQR 2·8-4·6] and
24|4·4 years [3·5-5·4], respectively) than in the ADT with
25|docetaxel population (3·0 years [2·1-3·8] and 3·8 years
26|[2·9-4·5], respectively). Regardless of the population and
27|survival outcome considered, the median follow-up
28|periods did not differ between the groups who did or did
29|not receive abiraterone. For the radiographic progression-
30|free survival analyses, the median follow-up periods
31|from randomisation to the cutoff date of Sept 1, 2020,
32|were 3·53 years for the overall population (3·52 years for
33|the SOC without abiraterone groups and 3·56 years for
34|the SOC plus abiraterone groups; log-rank p=0·86) and
35|2·99 years for the ADT with docetaxel population
36|(3·00 years and 2·97 years; log-rank p=0·93). For the
37|overall survival analyses, the median follow-up periods
38|from randomisation to the cutoff date of June 1, 2021,
39|were 4·41 years for the overall population (4·44 years for
40|the SOC without abiraterone groups and 4·39 years for
41|the SOC plus abiraterone groups; log-rank p=0·98) and
42|3·81 years for the ADT with docetaxel population
43|(3·75 years and 3·85 years; log-rank p=0·95).

7|for ECOG performance status, ADT type, and disease
8|burden. Consequently, the comparative evaluation of
9|abiraterone efficacy on survival outcomes was conducted
10|by pooling the groups two by two (SOC without
11|abiraterone [with or without radiotherapy] groups vs SOC
12|plus abiraterone [with or without radiotherapy] groups).
13|In the overall population, the addition of abiraterone to
14|SOC (with or without docetaxel and with or without
15|radiotherapy) decreased the number of radiographic
16|progression events or deaths from 371 to 252, improved
17|the median progression-free survival from 2·22 years
18|(IQR 1·09-6·03) to 4·46 years (1·72-not reached), and
19|reduced the relative risk of radiographic progression or
20|death by 46% compared with patients who did not receive
21|abiraterone (adjusted HR for radiographic progression-
22|free survival 0·54, 99·9% CI 0·41-0·71; p<0·0001;
23|figure 2A, table 2). The addition of abiraterone to SOC
24|(with or without docetaxel and with or without
25|radiotherapy) decreased the number of deaths from 268
26|to 228, improved the median overall survival from 4·72
27|years (IQR 2·59-not reached) to 5·72 years (2·72-not
28|reached), and reduced the risk of death from any cause by
29|18% (adjusted HR for overall survival 0·82, 95·1% CI
30|0·69-0·98; p=0·030; figure 2C, table 2). In the overall
31|population, the effect of abiraterone on radiographic
32|progression-free survival and overall survival showed a
33|high consistency across most of the predefined
34|subgroups, except for the under-represented subgroup of
35|patients who had bilateral orchiectomy and those who
36|did not receive docetaxel based on the investigator's
37|decision (figures 3A, 3C). For overall survival only, the
38|effect of the addition of abiraterone was pronounced in
39|patients with high-volume metastatic burden (figure 3C).
40|As SOC plus abiraterone showed a superior efficacy
41|compared with SOC without abiraterone that met the
42|required predefined significance level (type I error of
43|0·049 for overall survival and 0·001 for radiographic
44|progression-free survival) within the overall population,
45|abiraterone efficacy was further investigated within the
46|more restricted ADT with docetaxel population to assess
47|the preplanned coprimary endpoints. In this population,
48|compared with SOC (including docetaxel) without
49|abiraterone, the addition of abiraterone decreased the
50|number of radiographic progression events or deaths
51|from 211 to 139, improved the median radiographic
52|progression-free survival from 2·03 years (IQR 1·09-not
53|reached) to 4·46 years (1·90-not reached), and reduced
54|the relative risk of radiographic progression or death by
55|50% (adjusted HR for radiographic progression-free
56|survival 0·50, 99·9% CI 0·34-0·71; p<0·0001; figure
57|2B, table 2). Similarly, compared with SOC (including
58|docetaxel) without abiraterone, the addition of abira
59|terone reduced the number of deaths from 151 to 121,
60|improved the median overall survival from 4·43 years
61|(IQR 2·47-not reached) to not reached, and reduced the
62|relative risk of death from any cause by 25% (adjusted
63|HR for overall survival 0·75, 95·1% CI 0·59-0·95;
64|p=0·017; figure 2D, table 2).
